```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(dplyr)
library(flextable)

rd <- params$results_dir
img <- function(f) file.path(rd, f)
has_file <- function(f) file.exists(file.path(rd, f))

# Defensive coercion: guarantees these are numeric even if this file is
# ever knit directly (RStudio "Knit" button) instead of via
# R/07_generate_report.R, where the YAML defaults above would otherwise be
# used as-is.
pval_cutoff <- as.numeric(params$pval_cutoff)
lfc_cutoff  <- as.numeric(params$lfc_cutoff)

read_top <- function(f, n = 15) {
  if (!has_file(f)) return(NULL)
  df <- read.csv(file.path(rd, f))
  head(df, n)
}

# Formats small p/padj values as "<0.005" instead of long decimals.
format_pval <- function(x, threshold = 0.005) {
  ifelse(x < threshold, paste0("<", threshold), formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 4))
}

# Shared table style. p/padj columns get format_pval; other numeric
# columns get fixed decimal rounding. `title` adds a caption above the table.
nice_table <- function(df, digits = 4, title = NULL) {
  pval_cols <- names(df)[tolower(names(df)) %in% c("padj", "pvalue", "p_value", "pval")]
  for (col in pval_cols) df[[col]] <- format_pval(df[[col]])

  numeric_cols <- setdiff(names(df)[sapply(df, is.numeric)], pval_cols)
  ft <- flextable(df)
  if (length(numeric_cols) > 0) ft <- colformat_double(ft, j = numeric_cols, digits = digits)
  if (!is.null(title)) ft <- set_caption(ft, caption = title)
  ft <- theme_zebra(ft)
  ft <- autofit(ft)
  ft <- fontsize(ft, size = 10, part = "all")
  ft <- bg(ft, part = "header", bg = "#2c3e50")
  ft <- color(ft, part = "header", color = "white")
  ft
}
```

This report summarizes a transcriptomic analysis of `r params$project`, covering
differential expression, functional enrichment (GO, KEGG, Reactome), gene set
enrichment analysis (GSEA), and survival analysis for `r params$gene`.
Significance throughout is defined as adjusted p-value < `r pval_cutoff`,
with a |log2 fold change| >= `r lfc_cutoff` threshold for differential
expression.

## Sample Integrity Overview

```{r pca, results='asis'}
if (has_file("qc_pca.png")) {
  cat("The PCA plot below shows how samples separate along the first two ",
      "principal components of the variance-stabilized expression data. ",
      "Clear separation between Tumor and Normal samples supports the ",
      "validity of the downstream differential expression comparison.\n\n")
  knitr::include_graphics(img("qc_pca.png"))
} else {
  cat("_PCA plot not found -- run 03_deseq2_analysis.R first._")
}
```

```{r dispersion, results='asis'}
if (has_file("qc_dispersion.png")) {
  cat("\n\nThe dispersion plot checks whether DESeq2's variance model fit ",
      "the data well -- gene-wise estimates (black) should shrink toward ",
      "the fitted trend (red) to the final estimates used for testing (blue).\n\n")
  knitr::include_graphics(img("qc_dispersion.png"))
}
```

```{r poisson-dist, results='asis'}
if (has_file("qc_poisson_distance.png")) {
  cat("\n\nThis project has few or no Normal samples, so sample-to-sample ",
      "similarity is also checked directly on raw counts (Poisson distance), ",
      "independent of the Tumor/Normal grouping above.\n\n")
  knitr::include_graphics(img("qc_poisson_distance.png"))
}
```

## Differential Expression (DESeq2)

```{r deg-summary, results='asis'}
if (has_file("deseq2_results.csv")) {
  deg <- read.csv(file.path(rd, "deseq2_results.csv"))
  sig <- deg %>% filter(padj < pval_cutoff, abs(log2FoldChange) >= lfc_cutoff)
  cat(sprintf(
    "Of %d genes tested, **%d** were called significant (padj < %s, |log2FC| >= %s): %d upregulated, %d downregulated in Tumor vs Normal.\n\n",
    nrow(deg), nrow(sig), pval_cutoff, lfc_cutoff,
    sum(sig$log2FoldChange > 0), sum(sig$log2FoldChange < 0)
  ))
} else {
  cat("_DESeq2 results not found -- run 03_deseq2_analysis.R first._")
}
```

```{r volcano, results='asis'}
if (has_file("deg_volcano.png")) {
  cat("The volcano plot highlights the most significant differentially ",
      "expressed genes by adjusted p-value and fold change.\n\n")
  knitr::include_graphics(img("deg_volcano.png"))
}
```

```{r ma-plot, results='asis'}
if (has_file("qc_ma_plot.png")) {
  cat("\n\nThe MA plot checks for expression-level-dependent bias in the ",
      "results -- significant genes (colored) should appear across the ",
      "expression range, not just at low counts. Fold changes here may be ",
      "shrunken (see plot title) for display purposes; the DEG table and ",
      "CSV always report unshrunken values.\n\n")
  knitr::include_graphics(img("qc_ma_plot.png"))
}
```



### Top differentially expressed genes

```{r deg-table}
top_deg <- read_top("deseq2_results.csv", 20)
if (!is.null(top_deg)) {
  top_deg %>%
    arrange(padj) %>%
    head(20) %>%
    dplyr::select(gene_name, log2FoldChange, padj) %>%
    nice_table(title = "Top 20 differentially expressed genes")
}
```

## Functional Enrichment

Over-representation analysis (ORA) tests whether the significant DEGs are
enriched for specific biological pathways or processes, relative to all
tested genes as background. Separate results are shown for up- and
down-regulated genes across three reference databases: Gene Ontology (GO
Biological Process), KEGG, and Reactome.

### Upregulated genes

```{r enrich-up, results='asis'}
for (f in c("go_bp_upregulated.png", "kegg_upregulated.png", "reactome_upregulated.png")) {
  if (has_file(f)) cat(sprintf("![](%s)\n\n", img(f)))
}
```


### Downregulated genes

```{r enrich-down, results='asis'}
for (f in c("go_bp_downregulated.png", "kegg_downregulated.png", "reactome_downregulated.png")) {
  if (has_file(f)) cat(sprintf("![](%s)\n\n", img(f)))
}
```

## Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA)

Unlike ORA, GSEA uses the full ranked gene list (ranked by DESeq2 test
statistic) rather than only the genes that cross a significance threshold,
making it sensitive to coordinated shifts across a pathway even when no
individual gene is dramatically changed.

```{r gsea, results='asis'}
if (has_file("gsea_top_pathways.png")) {
  knitr::include_graphics(img("gsea_top_pathways.png"))
}
```

```{r gsea-table}
gsea_top <- read_top("gsea_results.csv", 15)
if (!is.null(gsea_top)) {
  gsea_top %>%
    dplyr::select(Pathway = pathway_label, NES, padj) %>%
    nice_table(title = "Top 15 enriched gene sets (GSEA)")
}
```
